content:
Belgian cleantech
company ARK Capture Solutions, which develops fully electric carbon capture
equipment for industrial emissions, has raised €5.4 million in a funding round
led by Aperam Ventures, with participation from existing shareholders Wallonie
Entreprendre, Noshaq, Invest.BW, Seeder Fund and BeAngels, alongside new
investors Encevo and VITO.

The investment
comes 20 months after the company's €2.2 million pre-seed round and marks its
transition from pilot testing to industrial-scale deployment.

Founded by Samuel Thiry and Aurélien Vantomme, ARK Capture Solutions focuses on developing more
affordable and energy-efficient alternatives to conventional industrial carbon
capture technologies.

The phase-out of
free carbon allowances and rising CO₂ prices under the EU Emissions Trading
System (ETS) are increasing demand for affordable carbon capture solutions.
Captured CO₂ can also be used in industrial production or, when derived from
biogenic sources, permanently stored to generate carbon removals.

However, flue gases
with CO₂ concentrations of between 4 and 20 per cent, estimated to account for
around half of global emissions, remain largely unaddressed due to the cost and
complexity of conventional capture technologies.

ARK aims to address
this challenge through its patented, fully electric and solvent-free hybrid
technology, which reduces energy consumption and capture costs while improving
operational safety. The technology is designed to complement existing decarbonisation
measures, such as energy efficiency, electrification and fuel switching,
particularly in industries where emissions are difficult or impossible to
avoid.

Since its pre-seed
round, ARK has successfully deployed and operated pilot units at three
industrial sites with varying flue gas compositions and CO₂ concentrations,
producing liquid CO₂ on-site that met the required specifications. In October
2026, the company completed a testing campaign at one of Belgium's largest
waste-to-energy plants.

ARK also leads CO₂
DISRUPT, a €5.6 million project supported by the Walloon Region, in
collaboration with Aperam, Industeel, Cinergie, UMONS and Certech. The project
aims to test a mobile unit capable of capturing 1,000 tonnes of CO₂ annually.

The company has
completed its first engineering and feasibility studies ahead of schedule and
is preparing to deliver its first commercial units. It is also expanding its
international reach, with ongoing discussions across Europe, Latin America,
Africa, Asia, North America and Oceania.

This round gives
us the means to move to the next scale and bring affordable carbon capture
technologies to the industries that need it most,

said Samuel Thiry and
Aurélien Vantomme, founders of ARK Capture Solutions.

The new funding
will support the industrial-scale deployment of ARK's technology at customer
sites and strengthen its engineering, supply chain and commercial capabilities
to meet growing demand across the steel, chemical, waste-to-energy, biogas and
other industrial sectors.
